front_blocks.md: Define **linear search**.

back_blocks.md: A linear search **starts with the first value** in a dataset and **checks every value one at a time** until all values have been checked.

cards.front_md: Define **linear search**.
cards.back_md: A linear search **starts with the first value** in a dataset and **checks every value one at a time** until all values have been checked.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A linear search requires the data to be in order.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A linear search can be performed **even if the values are not in order**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A linear search requires the data to be in order.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

A linear search can be performed **even if the values are not in order**.

front_blocks.md: In which order are elements checked in a linear search on an array?

back_blocks.md: In order from the **lower bound** to the **upper bound**, until the item is found or the upper bound is reached.

cards.front_md: In which order are elements checked in a linear search on an array?
cards.back_md: In order from the **lower bound** to the **upper bound**, until the item is found or the upper bound is reached.

front_blocks.md: What are the four steps of a linear search?

back_blocks.md: Check the first value. **IF** it is the value you are looking for, **STOP**. **ELSE** move to the next value and check. **REPEAT UNTIL** all values have been checked.

cards.front_md: What are the four steps of a linear search?
cards.back_md: Check the first value. **IF** it is the value you are looking for, **STOP**. **ELSE** move to the next value and check. **REPEAT UNTIL** all values have been checked.

front_blocks.md: Why does the linear search use a `WHILE` loop rather than a `FOR` loop?

back_blocks.md: For **flexibility**, because a `WHILE` loop allows an **early exit** as soon as the item is found.

back_blocks.md: `Index ← Index + 1`, which moves the search on to the next position.

front_blocks.md: Define **bubble sort**.

back_blocks.md: A bubble sort **checks values in pairs**, starting at the beginning of a dataset, and **swaps them if they are not in the correct order**.

cards.front_md: Define **bubble sort**.
cards.back_md: A bubble sort **checks values in pairs**, starting at the beginning of a dataset, and **swaps them if they are not in the correct order**.

front_blocks.md: Define **pass** in a bubble sort.

back_blocks.md: A pass is **one full run of comparisons from the beginning to the end** of the dataset.

cards.front_md: Define **pass** in a bubble sort.
cards.back_md: A pass is **one full run of comparisons from the beginning to the end** of the dataset.

front_blocks.md: When is a bubble sort finished?

back_blocks.md: When there are **no more swaps to make**.

cards.front_md: When is a bubble sort finished?
cards.back_md: When there are **no more swaps to make**.

front_blocks.md: What are the steps of a bubble sort?

back_blocks.md: Compare the first two values. **IF** they are in the wrong order, **swap them**. Compare the next two values and repeat to the end of the dataset. **IF** any swaps were made, repeat from the start. **ELSE** stop, because the list is in the correct order.
